dossier.public_summary: The dip looks flat (V~-3.1) and planet-sized on paper, but it appears strongly at different depths in each visit and even shows very different depths for odd versus even transits, which is typical of a binary eclipsing at twice the 14-day period. One sector shows no dip while others do, and individual transit depths are highly inconsistent, so a planet on the target is an unlikely explanation.

reasons.why: Odd (8555 ppm) and even (24450 ppm) depths differ strongly with ratio 2.9, the signature of an eclipsing binary folded at half its true period (28 d) rather than a planet at 14 d.
Depth changes by 140.1% between sectors, and per-sector depths show QLP sectors at ~28k-32k ppm but TESS-SPOC sector 19 at 671 +/-2102 ppm providing essentially no supporting transit.

QLP depth 29807 +/-1933 ppm steady within QLP (p_constant 0.660382362634522) but SPOC depth is undetected, indicating the signal is not present or not constant on the target as QLP-measured, consistent with a blend/bogus detection or sector-dependent systematics.

Single-transit depths are highly inconsistent (chi2 105.62, dof 4) with one shallow outlier at 588 +/- (~87 ppm) sigma -6.7 vs a deep 32066 ppm outlier at 4.9 sigma; share_of_top_3 1.0 shows signal dominated by few detections.
Planet-likelihood rank 0.06 is in the bottom decile where false positives dominate, corroborating odd/even and depth-inconsistency evidence.
